subject: Mercantile Law
question_text: Under the Contract Act 1872, which statement best describes 'consideration'?
option_a: A promise made without any return
option_b: A gift given out of natural love and affection only
option_c: Something done or abstained from at the desire of the promisor
option_d: A moral obligation arising from past voluntary service
explanation_detailed: Section 2(d) of the Contract Act defines consideration as an act, abstinence, or promise done or made at the desire of the promisor. Without lawful consideration, an agreement is generally not enforceable as a contract.
topic: Contract act sale of goods and partnership

subject: Mercantile Law
question_text: Under the Sale of Goods Act 1930, a stipulation collateral to the main purpose of the contract, the breach of which gives rise to a claim for damages but not rejection of goods, is called:
explanation_detailed: Section 12 distinguishes a condition from a warranty. Breach of a warranty allows damages only, while breach of a condition may allow rejection of goods and termination of the contract.

subject: Mercantile Law
question_text: Under Pakistani law, what is the maximum number of partners ordinarily permitted in a firm carrying on general business?
option_d: No statutory limit under the Partnership Act alone
explanation_detailed: Although the Partnership Act 1932 does not itself fix a maximum, company law in Pakistan limits a partnership in general business to 20 persons. For banking business, the limit is 10 partners.

subject: Mercantile Law
question_text: An agreement entered into by a minor under the Contract Act 1872 is:
option_a: Valid and enforceable against the minor
option_b: Voidable at the option of the other party only
option_c: Void ab initio as against the minor
option_d: Valid if ratified orally before attaining majority
explanation_detailed: Under Section 11 read with settled principles, a minor lacks contractual capacity, so an agreement with a minor is void as against him. A minor cannot be compelled to perform such an agreement.

subject: Mercantile Law
question_text: The general rule 'caveat emptor' under the Sale of Goods Act 1930 means:
option_c: The seller must disclose every hidden defect
option_d: The buyer may reject goods for any minor defect
explanation_detailed: Section 16 embodies caveat emptor, meaning the buyer must generally satisfy himself about quality and fitness unless an exception applies. The seller is not automatically liable for defects the buyer could have discovered by ordinary examination.

subject: Mercantile Law
question_text: Under Section 19 of the Partnership Act 1932, the act of a partner done in the name of the firm and in the usual way of business binds the firm if the partner acted:
option_a: Only with written authority signed by all partners
option_b: Within his implied authority as a partner
explanation_detailed: Every partner is an agent of the firm for business of the partnership. Acts done in the ordinary course of business within implied authority bind all partners even without express consent.
topic: Contract act sale of goods and partnership

subject: Mercantile Law
question_text: Under Section 56 of the Contract Act 1872, an agreement to do an act that becomes impossible or unlawful after it is made is:
option_a: Voidable at the option of the promisor
explanation_detailed: When performance becomes impossible or unlawful due to supervening events, the contract is discharged by frustration under Section 56. Such an agreement becomes void and parties are relieved from further performance.
topic: Contract act sale of goods and partnership

subject: Mercantile Law
question_text: Under the Sale of Goods Act 1930, 'specific goods' mean goods:
option_a: Goods manufactured after the contract is made
option_b: Goods identified and agreed upon at the time the contract is made
option_c: Goods selected from a large stock of similar articles
option_d: Goods ordered by description only without identification
explanation_detailed: Section 2(14) defines specific goods as goods identified and agreed upon at the time of the contract of sale. Unascertained goods become specific when they are appropriated to the contract with assent of both parties.
topic: Contract act sale of goods and partnership

subject: Mercantile Law
question_text: Which of the following is a ground for dissolution of a firm by the court under the Partnership Act 1932?
option_a: Permanent incapacity of a partner to perform his part
option_c: Increase in profit of the business
option_d: Admission of a new partner with consent of all
explanation_detailed: Section 39 lists grounds for court-ordered dissolution, including permanent incapacity, misconduct, persistent breach, transfer of whole interest, and business becoming unlawful. Routine disagreements or profitable operations are not grounds for dissolution by court.
topic: Contract act sale of goods and partnership

subject: Mercantile Law
question_text: Obligations resembling those created by contract, but arising without an agreement such as payment for necessaries supplied to a person incapable of contracting, fall under:
explanation_detailed: Chapter V of the Contract Act deals with certain relations resembling those created by contract. These quasi contracts prevent unjust enrichment, for example when necessaries are supplied to a minor or person of unsound mind.
